devices.notes: Source PDF is a scanned image with no text layer; all values were read visually from the page images (pages 7-22 of the PDF hold the SSED, pages 23-33 the device labeling). All table numbers were legible; none were lost. Film-screen device: films are digitized by a 50 micron laser digitizer and markers (triangle for microcalcification clusters, asterisk for masses) are shown on low-resolution images on a separate display; no more than three microcalcification ROIs or two mass ROIs per film. Three pivotal studies. Main coded test is Study 3A / Precision Study 1 (standalone sensitivity on 1,083 consecutive screen-detected cancers, 13 institutions, 1994-1996). Study 1 (Prospective Utilization Study): 14 MQSA-certified radiologists at 5 institutions, minimum 4 months pre- and 4 months post-installation; 23,682 cases read pre-installation and 14,817 post-installation; individual work-up rates 2.2-15.2% (mean 8.3%) pre vs 2.4-11.3% (mean 7.6%) post; the document states 'any change in call-back rates resulting from use of the device was too small to be detected'. This is a pre/post observational design, not a crossover reader study; the 'readers' field (14) comes from this study. Study 2 (Retrospective-Directed System Sensitivity Study): priors acquired 9-24 months before cancer detection from 13 institutions (1994-1996); 493 Priors collected, 141 'Invisible' excluded, 62 excluded for prior surgery or mastectomy, 4 excluded for oversight or unresolved history, 286 Visible Priors reviewed by panels of five radiologists in four case sets (each set approx. 75 visible priors, 5 invisible priors, 20 currents, 20 normals); Table 1: 0/5 consensus 28/83 (33.7%), 1/5 28/53 (52.8%), 2/5 24/38 (63.2%), 3/5 28/38 (73.7%), 4/5 30/38 (78.9%), 5/5 33/36 (91.7%); majority 3/5+ 91/112 (81.3%, CI 73.9-83.1%), super-majority 4/5+ 63/74 (85.1%, CI 76.9-87.5%), unanimous 33/36 (91.7%, CI 82.5-95.7%); Table 2 by feature for majority consensus: calcifications 37/39 (94.9%), masses 54/73 (74.0%). Study 3A Table 3: microcalcifications 396/404 (98.0%, CI 96.6-99.4%), masses 507/679 (74.7%, CI 71.3-77.9%), total 903/1083 (83.4%, CI 81.1-85.6%); marks per case 7.22 for cancers vs 3.58 for 100 normals. Study 3B (Precision Study 2): 25 cases (14 microcalcification, 11 mass), 50 films run 10 times on 3 systems, 1499/1500 correct (99.93%). Preliminary (non-pivotal) studies: a Corning HTA reader study of 5 certified radiologists (6-39 years experience) each reading 180 cancer-enriched cases from Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions, Baltimore, MD, with no statistically significant difference with vs without CAD; and a Palo Alto Medical Clinic (California) retrospective study of priors from 1993-1994 where 17 of 21 analyzable prior malignant microcalcification cases were marked. These are the only US locations named; no country is stated for the pivotal study sites, though participating radiologists were required to be 'MQSA Certified'. Labeling states the 1,083 cancers represent 'all cancers that were detected from a pool of approximately 250,000 asymptomatic screening mammograms' (an estimate from an assumed incidence, not a count). The labeling warns that breast density diminishes device sensitivity but gives no density breakdown of any study population. No race/ethnicity reported. No film or mammography unit vendor named. Five systems were installed at the five prospective-study institutions between February and May 1997. Radiological Devices Panel met May 11, 1998 and voted unanimously approvable; FDA required a postapproval study of true positive and false positive work-up rates. Marketed in Germany, Norway, Sweden, Finland, and France before US approval.

devices.notes: Applicant named in the document is CADx Medical Systems, Inc (U.S. agent Parexel; Mammagraph sample shows a Laval, Quebec, Canada address); the batch file lists the company as iCAD. Film-screen device: films are digitized by a laser digitizer and output is a paper printout (Mammagraph). Two studies, ROSE-1 and ROSE-2, both described as pivotal. The main coded test is ROSE-1D (standalone sensitivity on 930 screen-detected cancers from 17 institutions). Other components: ROSE-1M, 17 institutions enrolled 402 screening cases originally read normal/benign within 24 months before a cancer diagnosis; 377 had current and prior available; priors reviewed blinded by 3 panel radiologists, 313 recommended for work-up by at least one, 177 confirmed at the cancer location by 2 truthing radiologists ('Of these 177 missed cancer cases 62.7% were marked by the Second Look™'); an actionability multiplier (0/3 to 3/3 of panel) gave 80.3 cases and a denominator of 306 maximum retrospectively visible false negatives, hence 'at least 26.2%'. ROSE-1R: 25 cancer cases from ROSE-1D run 10 times on each of 3 systems, 745 of 750 correctly marked ('reproducibility was over 99%'). ROSE-2: prospective, 10 experienced mammographers at 5 institutions read 3,946 sequential screening mammograms unaided then with the Mammagraph; 657 vs 677 work-ups (16.6% vs 17.2%, 95% CIs 15.5-17.8% and 16.0-18.4%); 20 additional work-ups; historical work-up rate for the same radiologists 13.3% (516 of 3,876, CI 12.3-14.4%); estimated additional reading time 20% or less in 3,631 of 3,946 (92%) cases. The 'readers' field (10) is taken from ROSE-2, not from the main coded test. The non-clinical System Reliability paragraph says seven systems were installed at 'the seven (7) clinical trial sites participating in the prospective study between September 1999 and July 2000', whereas the ROSE-2 description says 5 institutions; the document does not reconcile this. The September 1999 to July 2000 window is the only date range given and applies to the prospective study, not to ROSE-1D. No country, age, race/ethnicity, or breast density is reported for any study population; no film or mammography unit vendor is named. Marketing history: Europe, Asia/Pacific, Australia and Canada. Not referred to the Radiological Devices Panel because the information 'substantially duplicates information previously reviewed by this panel'.
